column1: # The checks of shell/password.nsh. See check-shell-log.sh.
# A question beside the passwords of AMITSESetup or PlaintextPassword shows its value, one
# whose bytes overlap a password's shows none, and nothing shows a byte of a password

column3: .responses | length == 1 and .[0].selector == "8C78A505-BAA0-4C4A-869F-000000001100" and (.[0].question.answer | startswith("<ValueUnavailable: its bytes hold a password>"))
.responses | length == 1 and .[0].selector == "8C78A505-BAA0-4C4A-869F-000000001100" and (.[0].question.answer | startswith("<ValueUnavailable: its bytes hold a password>"))

any(.[]; .name == "Quiet Boot" and .answer == "Enabled") and any(.[]; .name == "Setting beside the password" and .answer == "5") and any(.[]; .name == "Password prefix as a number" and (.answer | startswith("<ValueUnavailable: its bytes hold a password>")))

column1: # set refuses to write in a HiiDB that declares a password question

column3: . == {"error_message": "this HiiDB declares a setup password question, and the UEFI Shell runs no setup browser, so no password is asked or checked; pass --i-am-fine-to-brick-this-system to write without it"}

. == {"error_message": "this HiiDB declares a setup password question, and the UEFI Shell runs no setup browser, so no password is asked or checked; pass --i-am-fine-to-brick-this-system to write without it"}

column1: # --bypass-setup-password is gone: it is an unexpected argument, as any unknown flag
# unless --i-am-fine-to-brick-this-system is given, which warns of the operation that it lifts

column3: ^warning: this HiiDB declares a setup password question, and the UEFI Shell runs no setup browser, so no password is asked or checked; --i-am-fine-to-brick-this-system lets uefisettings write without it$

. == {"error_message": "cannot set question \"Password prefix as a number\": EFI variable PlaintextPassword-8c78a505-baa0-4c4a-869f-000000001101 holds a password at bytes 0..16, which set never writes"}

column1: # unless --allow-volatile is given: 3 keeps the device path valid, and lasts until the next reset

column3: .responses | length == 1 and .[0].question.answer == "3 <volatile: lasts until the next reset or power cycle>" and .[0].modified == true
